tag: retiring stops being possible, so the only way out is a sink again
why: The option disappears and `--hand-to` is the only way to close an item holding routes — every area to ONE item, which is how P2.4 became a sink (nine of eleven rows arrived after its bar was written) and what the Owner's 2026-10-02 by-area ruling addressed. `if False and ...` leaves every message intact, so the leg must assert the BEHAVIOUR.

tag: an area another open item claims is retired anyway
why: THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION, and the reason this option is safe at all. Retiring an area an open item still claims ORPHANS work somebody owns — strictly worse than the sink it exists to avoid. The check uses route_row's own `exclude` set, so it asks the same question the register asks of every new row rather than a second rule that could disagree with it.

tag: the retirement is no longer reported
why: An area dropped from the routing table in silence is an area forgotten. The whole justification for retiring rather than handing on is that the consequence is RECORDED — a new row there is unscheduled and names its own slot — and a report nobody prints makes retiring indistinguishable from losing.

old: if to_finished and hand and args.retire_routes:
new: if False and hand and args.retire_routes:
why: They say opposite things about the same routes, so what happens to an area would depend on the order of the code rather than on what the caller asked for — and the caller would be told nothing. A command that silently picks between two contradictory instructions is how a register ends up in a state nobody chose.
